booster-t1-hip-waist.name: T1 hip roll/yaw and waist joint motor

booster-k1-hip-yaw-ankle.name: K1 hip yaw and ankle joint motor

robots.name: Asimov 1
robots.summary: Open-source 1.2 m, 35 kg biped humanoid for whole-body control and locomotion research, sold as a DIY kit with full BOM, CAD and a MuJoCo sim on GitHub. Rated for 5 kg per arm.

robots.name: G1
robots.summary: Compact 1.32 m, 35 kg humanoid with 23 joints (23 to 43 on the EDU version) driven by low-inertia internal-rotor PMSM joint motors. Unitree's spec sheet quotes a 90 N·m knee peak; its published URDF sets the knee and hip-roll limit at 139 N·m, which the joint map uses. About 2 hours of battery life.

joints.role: Hip pitch + hip yaw + waist yaw

robots.name: H2
robots.summary: Full-size 1.82 m, 70 kg humanoid with 31 DOF, up to 360 N·m at the leg joints and a bionic head. Arms carry about 7 kg rated, 15 kg peak.

robots.name: NEO
robots.summary: Home humanoid with tendon-driven actuation, a soft lattice-polymer body and 22-DOF hands. Weighs 30 kg and carries 25 kg.

robots.name: T1
robots.runtime_note: About 2 h walking, 4 h standing; retailer figure
robots.summary: Developer humanoid, 1.18 m and about 30 kg, with 23 DOF (31 with grippers, 41 with dexterous hands) and up to 130 N·m peak joint torque. Won RoboCup 2025 AdultSize. Joint-map torques are the effort limits in Booster's published URDF, which does not name the motor models.

joints.role: Waist yaw + hip roll + hip yaw

robots.name: K1
robots.runtime_note: 1 h 10 min on Edu and Pro; 20 min on the Geek edition
robots.summary: Entry-level 95 cm, 19.5 kg humanoid with 22 DOF, sold in Geek, Education and Professional editions. Won RoboCup 2025 KidSize. Booster's product page quotes up to 60 N·m peak joint torque, but its published URDF sets higher effort limits (knee 112 N·m, hip pitch 68 N·m); the joint map uses the URDF limits, which do not name the motor models.

joints.role: Hip yaw + ankle pitch + ankle roll

robots.name: Reachy 2
robots.summary: Open-source bimanual humanoid on an omnidirectional base, height adjustable from 1.36 to 1.66 m. Two 7-DOF arms carry about 3 kg each and a 3-DOF neck aims the head, all driven by Pollen's own Orbita parallel joints: 2-axis units at shoulder and elbow, 3-axis units at wrist and neck. Pollen publishes no list price; about $70k is the figure reported at launch.

robots.name: Reachy Mini
robots.runtime_note: Wireless has a 12.8 Wh pack rated 2 to 4 h depending on use; Lite runs on USB power
robots.summary: Open-source desktop companion robot from Pollen and Hugging Face, sold as a kit. A Stewart platform of six servos gives the head 6 DOF, with body rotation and two antennas on top. $399 Lite runs from a computer over USB; $499 Wireless adds a Raspberry Pi CM4 and battery.

robots.name: Manmaru YOR
robots.lead_time: Assembled by quote; DIY from the public BOM
robots.summary: Semi-humanoid for Physical AI research: two Seeed reBot Arm B601-DM arms (6 axes + gripper each, 767 mm reach, 1.5 kg payload) on the open-source YOR four-module swerve base. About $6,300 in parts to build from the published BOM and URDF, or about $12,700 assembled and tested. Seeed's BOM lists the Damiao motor mix per arm but not which joint gets which.

joints.role: Arm joints, higher torque (3 per arm)

robots.name: R1
robots.runtime_note: About 1 h per charge on all editions (R1 AIR, R1, R1 EDU); quick-release smart battery.
robots.summary: Unitree R1 is a 1.23 m, roughly 29 kg entry-level humanoid sold from $4,900 (R1 AIR, 20 DOF) and $5,900 (R1, 26 DOF), with an R1 EDU edition of 26 to 40 DOF sold through sales. Joints use Unitree's own low-inertia internal-rotor PMSM actuators with crossed roller bearings and dual encoders. Unitree publishes R1 URDF models in unitree_ros and R1 examples in the open unitree_sdk2.

robots.name: GR-3
robots.runtime_note: Hot-swappable packs (702 Wh + 234 Wh); 55 DOF counts the optional 12-DoF hands, 43 with the basic hands
robots.summary: Fourier GR-3 is a 165 cm, 71 kg care and companionship humanoid unveiled in August 2025, with a soft upholstered shell, 31 touch sensors, a four-microphone array and an LLM-driven interaction stack. It offers up to 55 DOF with optional 12-DoF dexterous hands, a 3 kg single-arm load, a 440 Nm maximum joint peak torque and about 3 hours of runtime. It is built on Fourier's own actuators and sold in GR-3, GR-3C and GR-3C Ultra configurations on quote.

robots.name: Digit 5
robots.runtime_note: 10:1 run-to-charge with a 9 min autonomous charge; no list price, reported S-4 terms are about $200k outright or $8,500/month RaaS
robots.lead_time: Early access expected H1 2027; general availability expected by end of 2027 (US, Canada, then EU and UK)
robots.summary: Digit 5 is Agility Robotics' fifth generation bipedal humanoid, unveiled September 15, 2026, for warehouse and manufacturing work alongside people without safety fencing. It stands 1.81 m, weighs 129 kg, lifts up to 22.7 kg (50 lb) repeatedly and reaches up to 2.2 m, with forward-facing legs driven by proprietary cycloidal actuators. A 90 minute battery recharges in 9 minutes, and the robot is sold by quote or as Robots-as-a-Service, with early access in H1 2027.

robots.name: YAM
robots.summary: Low-cost 6-DOF manipulator built for imitation learning and teleoperation data collection. CNC 6061 billet frame, integrated cross-roller bearings, 95 mm patent-pending gripper.

robots.name: YAM Pro
robots.summary: Same motor set and SDK as the base YAM; the control-law difference is a stiffer J4 position gain plus build refinements. Interchangeable with Standard and Ultra in the SDK.

robots.name: YAM Ultra 2
robots.summary: Enhanced build of the 6-DOF YAM with the same Damiao motor chain and SDK as Standard and Pro, tuned for higher-duty data collection.

robots.name: BIG YAM
robots.summary: Heavier-payload 6-DOF variant. Uses DM6248 motors at the shoulders with substantially different control gains and a reversed joint 2; the only YAM whose SDK gains differ meaningfully from Standard.

robots.name: YAM 7
robots.summary: 7-DOF member of the YAM family with an added redundant joint for richer wrist orientation. Unlike the rest of the family it runs on i2RT's own GF-series actuators (GF62X48 at the shoulder) rather than Damiao motors; i2RT has not published a joint-by-joint map.

robots.name: YAM Leader
robots.summary: Teleoperation leader arm: the operator backdrives it to puppeteer a follower YAM (GELLO-style). The SDK's leader mode drives a standard YAM arm config by default (DM4340 at J1-J3, DM4310 at J4-J6) with a teaching handle in place of the gripper.

robots.name: PiPER
robots.summary: PiPER is a 4.2 kg desktop 6-DOF arm from AgileX Robotics with a 1.5 kg payload, 626 mm reach and ±0.1 mm repeatability, built on an aluminum alloy frame with an integrated controller. It runs on DC 24V and is controlled over CAN, with drag teaching, trajectory replay, an open-source Python SDK, ROS 1/ROS 2 drivers and URDF models for Gazebo and Isaac Sim. A two-finger gripper (0 to 70 mm stroke, 40 N rated clamping force) and a teach pendant are optional end effectors.

robots.name: SO-101
robots.summary: SO-101 is an open-source, 3D-printable arm designed by TheRobotStudio with Hugging Face as the successor to SO-100, with improved wiring and easier assembly. The follower arm uses six Feetech STS3215 serial bus servos (5 arm joints plus a gripper) at a 1:345 gear ratio and is usually paired with a leader arm for teleoperation and imitation learning in the LeRobot library. STEP and STL files, simulation models and a full bill of materials are published under Apache-2.0, and kits are sold by Seeed Studio, WowRobo, PartaBot and others.

robots.name: Stretch 3
robots.runtime_note: 2 to 5 h per charge: 5 h at light CPU load, 2 h at high CPU load
robots.summary: Lightweight mobile manipulator: a 24.5 kg, 33 x 34 cm differential-drive base carries a 1.41 m mast with a lift, a telescoping arm reaching 0.52 m and a yaw-pitch-roll wrist, 7 manipulation DOF plus a compliant gripper and a pan-tilt head camera. Base wheels, lift and arm run on closed-loop steppers whose model Hello Robot does not name; wrist, gripper and head use Dynamixel servos. Listed at $24,950 until Stretch 4 took over in 2026.

robots.name: Franka Research 3
robots.summary: FR3 is the 7-DOF, force-sensitive research arm from Franka Robotics, with a link-side torque sensor in every joint, 3 kg payload, 855 mm reach and under ±0.1 mm repeatability. The open-source libfranka and Franka Control Interface give 1 kHz joint torque, position and velocity control, with ROS 2 and MATLAB support. Joint torque limits from the datasheet are listed below; Franka does not name its motors. Franka sells on quote; the price is Vention's catalog listing.
